memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And on the seventeenth day of the seventh month the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat. The waters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible. - Gen 8:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the tossing on a shoreless sea, the ark finally "came to rest." What a relief that word must have carried for Noah - solid ground beneath them at last, a firm place to settle after months adrift. The God who had carried them through the storm now brought them to rest.

But notice that resting did not mean everything was finished. The ark rested on the mountains, yet the waters kept receding for weeks more, and only slowly did the mountaintops appear. Noah found a resting place even while the full renewal was still unfolding. He could rest before the work was complete, because he rested on what God had provided.

This is a picture of the life of faith. We do not have to wait until every trouble is resolved to find rest. We can rest now - resting on God's finished provision even while we wait for the fullness of what He is doing. Rest is not the absence of unfinished business; it is trusting the One who holds the whole process in His hands.

Jesus offers this very rest: "Come to me... and I will give you rest" (Matt 11:28). In Him our souls find a resting place - a firm foundation beneath us - even while we wait for the day when all things are finally made new. Like the ark on Ararat, we can come to rest on solid ground long before the last of the waters have gone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you waiting for all your troubles to end before you let yourself rest?
- What would it mean to rest in Christ even now, before everything is resolved?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You bring me to rest on solid ground. Help me to rest in You now, trusting Your finished provision, even while I wait for all things to be made new.
